source.title: DecentLaM: Decentralized Momentum SGD for Large-batch Deep Training
source.authors: K. Yuan; Yi-Ming Chen; Xinmeng Huang; Ying-Ya Zhang; Pan Pan; Ying-Hui Xu; Wo-Tao Yin

record.tranche_reason: Reports batch-size results that refine the large-batch generalization claim, but its training schedule changes with batch size, so it does not test the fixed-epoch comparison directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation accuracy by batch size and method, plus training-loss and validation-accuracy curves. It does not report training-versus-test error gaps. Comparisons with cited prior studies are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: Tests V5 in decentralized image classification. The record overlooks fixed-budget comparisons: CIFAR-10 uses 200 epochs at both batch sizes; ImageNet uses 90 epochs for 2K versus 8K and 120 epochs for 16K versus 32K. Only comparisons across the 8K boundary change epoch budgets. Held-out accuracy suffices for V5; a training–test gap is unnecessary.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors attribute large-batch DmSGD degradation to momentum-amplified inconsistency bias and conclude that DecentLaM removes the additional momentum-induced bias, with theoretical convergence improvements and empirical performance gains. They do not claim to eliminate all inconsistency bias.
record.recipe_differences: Studies decentralized momentum methods and batch-size effects; it does not reproduce the fixed-epoch large-batch comparisons in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size, decentralized algorithm, model architecture, and network topology vary. The epoch budget and learning-rate schedule also differ between the small- and large-batch regimes.

fits_no_version.finding: DecentLaM improves decentralized optimization bias and often outperforms competing methods at a given batch size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing decentralized momentum updates reduces momentum-amplified inconsistency bias and improves optimization and validation performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Object-detection experiments compare methods at one total batch size, 256.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DecentLaM achieves slightly higher detection mAP than the evaluated baselines at batch size 256.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
record.problems: The large-batch schedule uses 120 epochs, while the small-batch schedule uses 90; therefore batch-size effects are not isolated at a fixed epoch budget. The paper reports validation accuracy rather than a training-to-test error gap.
record.rows_left_out: No rows kept. The batch-size results do not isolate the fixed-epoch comparison required by V5, and the paper reports no training-test error gap.

untested.parts: Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning regimes; LARS comparisons alone do not establish this.
Language models; isolated effects of longer training, warmup, normalization or regularization. ImageNet comparisons across the 8K boundary jointly change batch size, epochs and schedule.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.

missing.what: Restore the fixed-budget CIFAR-10 batch comparisons: PmSGD 91.6%→89.2% and DmSGD 91.5%→88.3%, 2K→8K, both 200 epochs. The blanket rows_left_out rationale incorrectly excludes these.

Restore within-regime ImageNet batch comparisons for all nine methods: 2K versus 8K at 90 epochs and 16K versus 32K at 120 epochs. Cross-regime comparisons require a schedule-confounding qualification.

Restore architecture-specific 2K versus 8K comparisons at 90 epochs in Table 4, including MobileNet-v2's mostly improving accuracy and ResNet-18 QG-DmSGD's 70.2%→70.5%. These establish workload and method dependence. ResNet-50 duplicates Table 3.

record.verdict_notes: No existing rows require correction because the record contains none. Its exclusion of all batch-size evidence is unjustified. The study is not an original source for V5. Numerical differences are descriptive: the supplied tables do not report uncertainty or significance tests.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under different tuning regimes.
The paper varies batch size and reports validation accuracy, but changes the epoch budget by batch-size regime; it does not isolate a fixed-epoch batch-size effect. Language models are not tested.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, ResNet-20, batch 2K versus 8K, 200 epochs, linearly scaled learning rate with warmup
relationships.reason: Table 1 and Appendix G.1 show validation accuracy falling from 91.6% to 89.2% for PmSGD and 91.5% to 88.3% for DmSGD. Verdict uses text; no rows were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: Validation accuracy was lower for PmSGD and DmSGD at the larger batch, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: ImageNet, ResNet-50, batch 16K versus 32K, 120 epochs with warmup and cosine scheduling
relationships.reason: Table 3 shows lower validation accuracy for all nine methods: PmSGD falls 76.27%→75.27%, DmSGD 76.23%→74.97%, and DecentLaM 76.73%→76.22%. Verdict uses text; no rows were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: Validation accuracy was lower for every tested method, including DecentLaM, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.reason: Table 3 shows lower validation accuracy for all nine methods, including PmSGD 76.32%→76.08%, DmSGD 76.27%→75.96%, and DecentLaM 76.43%→76.19%; several decreases are small. Verdict uses text; no rows were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: Validation accuracy was lower across the tested methods, sometimes by small amounts, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.reason: Table 4 shows accuracy increasing for eight of nine methods, including PmSGD 70.6%→71.1% and DecentLaM 70.3%→71.4%; this range does not show a batch penalty for those recipes. Verdict uses text; no rows were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy reportedly increased for eight of nine methods, but these comparisons remain unverified. They do not identify a batch size above which accuracy falls.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
